Hi Nora —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we discussed, the next 2 weeks are focused on getting you to a stable production profile with predictable token cost and tail latency under 200ms p95 for your primary chat route. I put together a concise checklist we can work through in our implementation sprint: batching strategy, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile selection per model variant, and routing policies (primary/backup/pricing tiers).

Attached: onboarding checklist (spreadsheet) and a small sample traffic profile we can use to simulate your distribution. Can you confirm the following by EOD Tuesday?
- A representative sample of 1% of your daily traffic (anonymized) — we can accept the JSON format in the attached sample template.
- The three models you want to evaluate for the first rollout (name + expected max sequence length).
- Any hard SLA constraints (p50/p95) beyond the baseline we discussed.

Plan I propose:
1) Monday (this week): we ingest sample traffic and run a quick profile run (Monica owns).
2) Tuesday–Wednesday: batching/caching experiments (Monica + Aditya).
3) Thursday: quantization profile A/B test against quality baseline (Aditya).
4) Following week: routing policy rollout and canary (Vanessa to coordinate with your infra).

We can use the Drive doc I shared for live notes: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDefG-onboard-playbook

If that cadence works, I’ll send calendar invites and a short mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz

Nora / Vanessa —

Quick update after profiling the sample you dropped in this morning (thanks, Nora). Key findings from a 10k-sample pass:
- Traffic distribution: 68% short queries (<256 tokens), 22% mid (256–1024), 10% long (>1024).
- KV cache hit rate potential: ~35% if we enable prefix caching on chat-1 route. That maps to an estimated 12–18% token cost reduction for typical sessions.
- Batching headroom: with our recommended batch size (dynamic up to 48) we saw 25–40% throughput improvement for mid-length sequences without p95 regressions in CPU-bound tests.

Immediate proposals (for this sprint):
1) Batching: start with conservative dynamic batch sizing capped at 32 for chat-1; capture latency heatmaps.
2) Caching: enable prefix KV caching for sessions flagged with a stable conversation id; we’ll instrument hit-rate telemetry and toggle in canary.
3) Quantization: run two profiles — 8-bit quant (fast) vs 6-bit hybrid (size-focused). We’ll run the 5 prompt quality checks Nora requested and produce a simple rouge-like metric + manual check notes.
4) Routing: configure primary to the higher-accuracy variant, fallback to the faster quantized variant when queue depth exceeds threshold or cost budget triggers. We’ll surface routing rules in the policy doc.

Can everyone review and confirm: batch cap 32, enable prefix caching in canary, run both quant profiles and post quality checks. I’ll attach the experiment run commands and the small script we used to generate the heatmaps.

—Monica
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
